text:
sasha: Heads up — I want to follow up on the pool orchestration split we discussed in the RFC. Specifically thinking about separating "lifecycle responsibilities" so the operator owns VM/GPU lifecycle and control-plane owns admission/intent. I'm worried about gaps in telemetry and racey transitions.

ben: +1 to splitting responsibilities, but can we be explicit about transition events? operator needs to emit: `POOL_READY`, `POOL_DRAINING`, `POOL_FAILED`, `POOL_SCALE_COMPLETE`. control-plane should react to those, not assume state.

maria: Those events sound good. Also we need a heartbeat with capacity estimates (available_slots, estimated_warmup_ms) — otherwise admission makes bad decisions.

oliver: Agree. Another tradeoff: who owns prewarm credits? If operator keeps prewarm bookkeeping, control-plane cannot fairly charge tenants. If control-plane owns tokens, operator may have to honor cancellations mid-startup.

kevin: From infra ops POV, operator should control physical resources + warmup ordering; control-plane keeps accounting and policy. Signals we should add to the operator API: `reserve_headroom(tenant, slots) -> reservation_id` and `release_reservation(reservation_id)` so control-plane can coordinate billing and rollbacks.

ben: That API works but add an idempotency token and an ETA field for warmup. Also an explicit `abort_warmup(reservation_id)` that guarantees operator will stop provisioning and free underlying resources within X ms.

sasha: Good. On telemetry: operator must export granular metrics (per-pool): `slots_total`, `slots_ready`, `slots_warming`, `avg_warmup_ms`, `last_scale_duration_ms`, and an event log stream for lifecycle events. We should define prometheus metric names and labels now.

maria: We currently only get coarse node counts, not slot-level. That causes the control-plane admission to overprovision. I'll draft a Prometheus scrape/labels proposal.

oliver: There's also the evictions model — when control-plane tells operator to drain, operator needs a policy: immediate kill vs graceful drain (inflight requests). We need a drain window + admission backoff guidelines.

kevin: Suggest default drain behavior: start-backoff=10s, notify-control-plane: `drain_started(pool, expected_completion_ts)`, then `drain_complete(pool)`. Add a `drain_progress` gauge.

ben: Edge case: multi-tenant warmup collisions. If two tenants both reserve headroom and operator picks order, who gets billed if capacity only fits one? Control-plane must decide allocation policy (fair-share, priority). Operator should accept a sorted reservation list and honor FIFO for identical priority.

sasha: Right. Let's also define fallback behavior when operator capacity lags for N seconds: control-plane should automatically route to fallback model variant (cheaper/slower) rather than queue forever. We'll parameterize `max_wait_ms` per tenant/SLO.

maria: Can we add a lightweight `reservation_state` webhook so control-plane can receive push updates instead of polling? Polling every 5s is painful.

oliver: Webhooks are ok but must be signed. Also require idempotent receipts because retries will happen.

kevin: Implementation note: operator already has a leader-elected control loop; adding reservation RPCs is cheap. The harder part is guaranteeing warmup latencies across heterogeneous GPUs; we need a calibration job that reports model-specific warmup profiles to control-plane.

ben: Calibration is key. Propose a `warmup_profile` JSON blob per model (cold_ms_mean, cold_ms_p95, kv_cache_restore_ms) that operator uploads after first boot or periodically. Control-plane can use that to compute ETA.

sasha: Action items: 1) ben — draft operator RPC contract w/ idempotency and events (deadline: EOD Fri). 2) maria — prometheus metric names + labels (deadline: Tue). 3) oliver — design reservation lifecycle diagram + failure modes (deadline: Tue). 4) kevin — feasibility check + rough infra cost estimate for signed webhooks (deadline: Mon).

maria: I'll also add a proposal for a `fallback_model` routing knob in the admission API.

ben: Quick question: how do we handle partial failures where operator reports `POOL_SCALE_COMPLETE` but some slots are `failed_warmup`? We should make `pool_scale_result` include counts: `{ready, warming, failed}`.

kevin: Yes, operator should emit both events and a final result payload. That helps billing reconcile.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: `staging/operator-v2` -> Mon 09:00UTC (will add new metrics endpoints behind feature flag).

sasha: Nice. One more thing — rollback plan: if the new contract causes admission regressions, control-plane will flip a `use_v2_operator_api=false` flag in feature flags and fall back to polling-mode. We should document toggles and a canary plan.

oliver: I'll add a small test harness that simulates slow warmup and reservation races for canary.

maria: ok I'll start the prometheus PR and link it in the doc. Link to RFC: https://r.redwood/proposals/pool-lifecycle-split

ben: thanks — will ping when RPC draft is ready.

kevin: Ping me if you need infra quotas for staging.

sasha: Cool — thanks everyone. We'll sync next Thurs for a follow-up.
